name: Tricolor Strawberry Begonia
description: Saxifraga stolonifera 'Tricolor' is a variegated cultivar of the strawberry begonia (creeping saxifrage), a stoloniferous perennial in the Saxifragaceae family native to China, Japan, and Korea. Despite its common name, it is neither a begonia nor a geranium. The cultivar features smaller round to heart-shaped leaves with green centers, creamy-white to yellow margins, and pink flushes that intensify in bright light; undersides are often reddish. Thin red stolons carry plantlets at their tips, similar to strawberry runners. It prefers bright indirect light, evenly moist but well-drained soil, and cooler indoor temperatures (about 15–24 °C). Excellent for hanging baskets and terrariums. Generally considered non-toxic to pets and humans.
careTips: Bright indirect light keeps variegation strong; avoid harsh midday sun that fades or scorches leaves
Keep soil lightly moist; allow the top 2–3 cm to dry between waterings; reduce water in cool winter rest
Use well-draining, organically rich mix; never leave the pot sitting in water
Moderate humidity (40–60%); use a pebble tray if air is dry — do not mist hairy leaves
Prefers cooler rooms (15–24 °C); protect from heat and cold drafts
Propagate by pinning stolon plantlets into moist soil until rooted, then sever from the mother plant
Generally non-toxic and suitable for homes with pets
geographicOrigin: East Asia (China, Japan, Korea) — cultivar of horticultural origin
